changelog: - **A Gate now shows what it did with each step: a small state light at its top-left corner, and a line in the Inspector that says why.** Until now a reader saw only the amounts that moved, so a Gate that passed on a part, one held back by its `pull all` rule, and one with nothing to pass looked the same. After a step the light reads: a filled green disc when the Gate passed on all it could take; a half-filled yellow disc when it passed on a part; a yellow ring with a bar across it when there was something to pass and it moved nothing (its all-or-nothing demand was not met, its outlet had no room, or the group it runs with moved nothing); a red disc beside the `!` flag when a reason names the Gate itself (invalid branch weights, a cycle with no storage); and the outline only when there was nothing to pass — a normal zero is not a warning — or the Gate did not run this step. Every state is a shape as well as a colour, nothing blinks, and the light follows your high-contrast setting. Select the Gate and the Inspector says the state in words, why, and the numbers: what it moved, of what it would have moved with nothing in the way, against what its inputs held. That demand is the Gate's own — a Gate whose group plan cut its share reads as a part, never as full — and a `pull all` Gate whose upstream could deliver no more is "supplied in part": it took all it was offered. The engine reports this as data (`StepReport.gates`); the amounts that move do not change, so every bundled example runs exactly as before.
